topic.title: What Happens After Suggesting Changes
topic.shortdesc: A review task created by a Contributor has no owner until a project maintainer or owner takes it over and drives it to completion.

body.p: Usually, the user who creates a review task becomes its owner. However, a task created by a Contributor has no owner because Contributors cannot integrate changes into a project. The task waits for someone who can.

section.title: What Happens to Your Task

ol.li: All project maintainers and owners, who can own review tasks, receive an email notification that you created a task that needs an owner.
One of them opens the task and clicks Assign Me as Owner. From that point, they own the task and manage the review.
You receive an email notification that tells you who took the task over.
The new owner runs the review, and can integrate the accepted changes into the project.

section.p: Until someone takes ownership, the task remains in the project's list of review tasks without an owner. If no one takes ownership, contact a project maintainer or owner directly.

section.title: Your Role in the Task
section.p: You participate in the task you created as a Reviewer. The task remains in your list of review tasks. You can continue editing its files, answer other participants' questions, and follow the discussion.
Only the task owner can manage it: change its settings, share it with other users, close the review, and integrate the changes.
